home.description: Daniel Burger's 30 meditations on synthetic consciousness and hybrid mind uploading, in Descartes' sense: one question worked through each day, not settled claims.

0-the-start.description: Day 0 of 30: why I am working through my ontology of synthetic consciousness and hybrid mind uploading in public, one item a day, as Cartesian meditations.

1-causa-finalis.description: Day 1 of 30, the vision: why synthetic consciousness, rather than artificial or machine consciousness, names a consciousness that no longer has to end.

2-hybrid-mind-uploading.description: Day 2 of 30, the mission: hybrid mind uploading versus classical mind uploading and whole brain emulation, and what "hybrid" means for the process world-line.

3-solving-death.description: Day 3 of 30: why I want to solve death, cause versus reason, the lightbulb analogy and where it breaks, and the deprivation view of why death is bad for the one who dies.

4-measurements-models-theories.description: Day 4 of 30: the second goal of the Ontology, understand consciousness, and why measurement comes before models and models before any theory of what consciousness is.

5-transcending-biology.description: Day 5 of 30: the third goal of the Ontology, renamed "transcend humanity": going beyond the limits that human biology sets for us, while the limits of physics stay where they are.

6-substrate-independence.description: Day 6 of 30: the first outcome of the Ontology, substrate independence, and why I mean physical rather than computational substrate independence: independent of biology, never of physics.

7-augmented-cognition.description: Day 7 of 30: the second outcome of the Ontology, augmented cognition, and why augmentation comes last: a baseline first, so we can see what changed.

8-collective-mind.description: Day 8 of 30: the third and last outcome of the Ontology, collective mind. Who says that we stay individuals, and don't merge into one collective mind?

9-multiple-realisability.description: Day 9 of 30: the first requirement of the Ontology, multiple realisability, in a weak form (living tissue takes over) and a strong one (de novo tissue).

10-continuer-migration.description: Day 10 of 30: the second requirement, continuer migration, and the only thing that I care about deeply: the continuity of the human brain.

11-morphological-independence.description: Day 11 of 30: morphological independence. Who says that a mechanistic neuron is literally the same size as the biological neuron that it replaces?
11-morphological-independence.video_description: Animation in five stages, Biological, Biohybrid, Biomimetic, Mechanistic and Smaller: one neuron in the whole brain is replaced until it runs at half the route length and half the carrier speed, so every delay (route length / carrier speed) is kept on the process world-line.

12-distributed-unification.description: Day 12 of 30: distributed unification. Every brain is already distributed, yet unified. How far can this be stretched, and what does the stretching?
12-distributed-unification.video_description: Animation: the two halves of a brain pulled apart, from your brain today (15 cm, callosal axons) across a continent and a planet to a solar system (4.5 billion km, light), with how many exchanges fit in one now and how long one now lasts at each distance.
12-distributed-unification.continued: The rest of this meditation will be posted soon.
